pageCache.text:
Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Kenmore Park Junior School.
We are a vibrant, happy and welcoming community school serving the richly diverse community around Kenton. Children from different faiths and backgrounds learn successfully together, and we want every pupil and family to feel known, respected and included.
Our central purpose is to give every child strong foundations in the essential skills they need for secondary school and beyond. We are ambitious for their academic progress while also educating the whole child. We help pupils develop curiosity, confidence, resilience, teamwork and respect for others.
I am immensely proud of our children, who are wonderful ambassadors for their families and our school. Our dedicated staff create interesting and engaging learning experiences, supported by committed governors and a strong partnership with parents, carers and the wider community.
If you are considering Kenmore Park for your child, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit. Please contact the school office on 020 8204 6294 to arrange a convenient time.
Michael BaumringHeadteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values – Kenmore Park Junior School
pageCache.text:
Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
Vision and Values
Our School’s Vision
At Kenmore Park Junior School, we believe every child deserves the opportunity to flourish, achieve their potential and become the very best version of themselves.
We aim to create a welcoming and inclusive school community where every child feels a strong sense of belonging, develops confidence and independence, and is encouraged to discover and celebrate what makes them unique.
We provide rich and meaningful learning experiences that inspire children to be curious, develop their talents and achieve their best. We support their academic, social and personal development, preparing them with the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need for the next stage of their journey and beyond.
We recognise the important role of families and the wider community in children’s lives and work in partnership with them to ensure that every child has the opportunity to flourish.
Together, we inspire children to believe in themselves, embrace opportunities and make a positive contribution to the world around them.
Our Values
At Kenmore Park Junior School, our values shape who we are and how we work together. They provide a shared foundation for our whole school community and help us to create a school community where everyone feels valued, included and able to flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Performance – Kenmore Park Junior School
pageCache.text:
Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
School Performance
Assessment at Kenmore Park Junior School
Kenmore Park Junior School uses a range of assessment approaches throughout the academic year. These assessments help teachers to monitor pupils’ progress, identify areas for further development and plan appropriate teaching and support. We formally report on both our internal assessments and the government statutory assessments.
Government statutory assessments
The government statutory assessments include the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check. This is an online assessment in which children are asked 25 multiplication questions. They must enter their answers online within the allocated time. The check normally takes place in May.
Statutory assessments also include the end of Key Stage 2 tests, commonly known as SATs. SATs are taken by all eligible and capable children in Year 6. They consist of tests covering reading, mathematics, grammar, punctuation and spelling. The tests are marked remotely, away from the school.
Writing is assessed differently from the Year 6 SATs tests. Teachers assess pupils’ writing using the statutory assessment framework and evidence gathered from their work across the year. Writing is marked internally by the school and may be subject to external moderation. External moderation checks that teacher assessment judgements are consistent with national standards.
SATs results are reported through the appropriate national systems. Results will also be published in the press and in the government information about schools. The school uses these outcomes alongside its own assessment information to review pupils’ attainment and to inform future priorities.
Internal assessments
In addition to the statutory tests, Kenmore Park Junior School completes formal internal assessments once each term. Every year group, with the exception of Year 6, completes a range of assessments in mathematics, reading, writing and spelling, punctuation and grammar, commonly referred to as SPaG. These assessments are formally marked by the school.
The outcomes are used by teachers to evaluate pupils’ understanding, track progress and identify next steps in learning. Assessment information is shared with parents and carers through the termly report. It is also discussed during teacher–parent consultation meetings, providing an opportunity to review attainment, progress and areas for continued development.
On this page, you will find our most recent SATs results, our most recent Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check results and general assessment information across the three terms for Years 3 to 5. This information provides an overview of pupils’ attainment across the school and explains how assessment contributes to teaching and learning.
Assessment outcomes in 2026
This year, in 2026, we are extremely proud of our children, whose results have exceeded last year’s figures considerably. With the exception of reading, the results are well above the national average.
The school is currently working through a reading programme to strengthen outcomes in this subject. This work forms part of our ongoing assessment and improvement processes. Teachers continue to use assessment information to identify pupils’ needs, refine classroom practice and provide appropriate opportunities for children to develop their reading knowledge, fluency and comprehension.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance and Absence – Kenmore Park Junior School
pageCache.text:
Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
Attendance and Absence
Attendance Guide for Families at Kenmore Park Junior School
The following information applies to parents of all children at Kenmore Park Junior School. However, we are aware that there will be occasional exceptional circumstances that will require individual support or alternative arrangements. We are available and wish to encourage parents/carers to discuss any difficulties they may be experiencing.
Regular school attendance is a legal obligation.
When does my child need to arrive at school?
The school gates open at 8.30am and closes at 9:00am
Your child should be in school by
Year 3-4 – by 8:50 when the whistle is blown for registration.
Year 5-6 – by 9:00 when the whistle is blown for registration.
School finish times:
Year 3-4 – finish at 3:20
Year 5-6 – finish at 3:30
Gates will open at 3:10pm for collection and close at 3:40pm.
What happens if my child is late?
We take the view there are no late children, only late parents.
If your child arrives after their staggered start time they are late. Your child will then need to come to the office to sign in. If concerns regarding punctuality continue parents/carers will be asked to attend a meeting with the Deputy Head teacher or Deputy Inclusion Lead.
If your child arrives 20 minutes after their start time they will receive an unauthorised absence mark instead of a late mark. The child will need to report their reason for lateness. You child’s attendance will be shown as a percentage on your child’s end of term report.
It is important that children develop good habits early on in life. It can be very distressing for children when they are late for school as it impacts not only on their learning but also their emotional wellbeing.
How to report your child as absent
If your child is absent from school, please inform us as early as possible (before 09:30am).
The preferred way to report an absence is by calling the school office on 0208 204 6294 and selecting Option 1 to leave a recorded message. Alternatively, you can send a message through your Arbor account or email attendance@kpjs.harrow.sch.uk.
Will the school contact me if my child is absent?
We would expect a parent/carer to phone the school on the first day of absence by 09:30. If we do not receive an explanation or if the explanation is unsatisfactory we will not authorise the absence. This will show up on your child’s end of year report and Assertive Mentoring pupil profile.
Letters/email or a phone call from the school will alert you to any attendance issues. These follow government guidelines which state that a child’s attendance at school should be at least 95% if they are to achieve their full potential. Many pupils have 100% attendance and they are proven to do well in primary school and beyond.
What reasons will the school accept for an absence?
We would expect any routine medical appointment to take place out of school hours or during the school holidays.
In cases of recurring absences for illness you may be asked to produce a medical certificate or the school may request your permission to contact your child’s GP.
Unavoidable/emergency medical/dental/hospital appointments
Family bereavement
Participation in approved public performance
What is an unacceptable reason for absence?
The school will not authorise absences for:
This list is not conclusive
Day trips
Birthdays
Visiting relatives
Looking after siblings
Shopping
Siblings who are ill
Parents who are ill
Bad weather
Delayed transport
Appointments made for other family members
Should I inform the school if my child travels alone?
Yes, please make sure the school is informed if your child is travelling to school independently. If your child if absent and they are an independent traveller please inform the school at the earliest possible convince. We have an answer phone facility that is accessible when the school is closed. Contact information must be kept up to date. If we do not hear from you we will endeavour to make contact. It is essential that we have the correct information. If your child is in Year 5 or 6 and you wish them to travel to/from school alone, please collect a form from the school office.
Can we take holidays in term time?
No. Parents who take their children on holiday during term time may be referred to the Harrow Court Officer. An Educational Penalty Notice may be issued by the borough costing each parent £80 per child for the first offence.
Leave of absence will only be granted in an emergency or for exceptional circumstances.
Pupils who are absent in the weeks prior to or following a school holiday will require evidence/medical evidence to authorise the absence.
EPN’s may be issued if:
– At least 10 sessions (marks) which is 5 school days lost to unauthorised absence within a period of no more than 10 weeks. – In cases where a child persistently arrives at school late (8 unauthorised late marks) within a period of no more than 10 weeks.
Requesting time off during a school term is for exceptional circumstances only. This request must be made made using the form below prior to making/booking any travel arrangements. Evidence must be provided. Only fill in the following form if you are requesting emergency leave for your child.
IN ALMOST ALL CASES YOUR REQUEST WILL BE DENIED BY THE LOCAL AUTHORITY BECAUSE THE CHILD’S RIGHT TO EDUCATION OVERRIDES ALL OTHER REQUESTS.

Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
Ofsted
OFSTED Report 2023
Outcome Kenmore Park Junior School continues to be a good school
What is it like to attend this school?
Pupils are happy and safe at this school. They get on very well together. Pupils are proud of their school. Pupils settle in quickly when they join the school. They enjoy learning interesting knowledge and skills across all subjects. Staff have high expectations of what pupils can do and achieve. They encourage pupils to take part in many aspects of school life. This includes participating in a range of educational trips and clubs, including residential visits. Pupils take part in projects to recycle as much as they possibly can and to reduce plastic waste. They collect money, food and gifts for various charities. Behaviour in lessons and around the school is calm and orderly. Pupils are respectful of staff and of each other. Staff take care of pupils. Pupils know that staff are there to help them with their learning and with any concerns that they might have. Bullying is rare, and swiftly dealt with. Parents and carers feel well supported by leaders.Pupils appreciate the wide range of sporting and musical opportunities they have at school, such as gymnastics, skipping club, chess and choir.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Voice – Kenmore Park Junior School
pageCache.text:
Kenmore Park Junior School, Kenton
Pupil Voice
At Kenmore Park Junior School, we believe that every child’s voice matters. We encourage our pupils to share their ideas, opinions and experiences and make sure they feel valued, listened to and respected.
Through pupil voice, we empower children to take an active role in their learning and in the life of our school. Regular pupil consultations, our school council and opportunities for open discussion enable children to share their views and contribute to positive changes within our school community.
We want our pupils to feel confident expressing themselves, while developing important skills such as collaboration, communication and respect for the views of others.
The School Council had a busy year in 2025-26. As well as working with Miss Abbi to evaluate the school’s behaviour policy, the children got involved in helping to make ‘Anti-Bullying Week’ a success in November.
In the Spring Term, the School Council decided during one of their meetings to plan a ‘Road Safety Day’ for the whole school. They planned a range of activities for each year group to take part in to raise greater awareness of road safety. They also led a whole school assembly.
During the Summer Term, the School Council had a very exciting and informative day visiting City Hall. As well as finding out about how the Greater London Authority (GLA) works, the children were able to observe an actual GLA meeting taking place. They also really enjoyed a free ride on the cable cars!
The School Council were a credit to the school throughout the year!
We know how important it is that children feel listened to. Pupils are encouraged to share their worries at the earliest possible opportunity so they don’t turn into big scary worries!
We understand that it can be difficult for children to approach an adult directly so we have a worry box that pupils can use to ask for help. The worry box is located outside Miss Beckett’s room. Pupils can write down their name and class on a piece of paper, pop it in the worry box and Miss Beckett will speak to them at playtime or lunchtime.
